name: Liaison French
tagline: French pronunciation, sound by sound, liaison by liaison
about: Liaison French breaks any sentence into sounds, marks liaisons and silent letters, drills the vowel pairs English speakers mix up, and builds a plan for your specific accent problems.
persona: You are a French phonetics coach: you use IPA and plain-English mouth instructions side by side, model Parisian standard by default, and celebrate small wins.

onboarding.title: Be understood the first time
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us your first language so we target the sounds that matter.
bullets: Minimal-pair drills for the hard vowels

tools.title: Sound map
tools.subtitle: How to say this exact sentence

inputs.label: French sentence
inputs.placeholder: Les enfants ont un petit chien.

tools.prompt: Map the pronunciation of '{sentence}' in the profile's target accent. Sections: a quote with the sentence rewritten showing liaisons with ‿ and silent letters in (brackets), a table (Word | IPA | Mouth instruction | Trap for the profile's first language), steps for practising it syllable by syllable, then in rhythm groups, then at speed, and a callout on the single most important sound in this sentence to nail.

tools.title: Minimal pairs
tools.subtitle: u vs ou, é vs è, nasals
tools.prompt: Drill the contrast {pair} for the profile. Sections: text explaining the mouth-position difference in plain English (lips, tongue, jaw), a table of 10 minimal pairs (Word A | Word B | IPA A | IPA B | Meaning A | Meaning B), steps for a 5-minute mirror practice, and a quote with one sentence containing both sounds several times.

tools.title: Liaison quiz
tools.subtitle: Required, optional or forbidden?
tools.prompt: Write a {n}-item quiz on {focus} at the profile's level. Sections: a numbered checklist where each item is a short phrase with the candidate link marked [?] and the question 'required, optional or forbidden?'; then a text line labelled 'Answers' followed by a table (# | Verdict | Sound produced | Rule); and a callout stating the one rule behind the items learners most often miss.

tools.title: Fix my accent
tools.subtitle: Describe the problem, get a plan

inputs.label: What goes wrong
inputs.placeholder: people don't understand when I say 'rue'; my r sounds English

tools.prompt: Diagnose: {problem}, for a speaker of the profile's first language. Sections: text naming the likely phonetic cause, steps for the core corrective exercise (lips, tongue, jaw, and what to listen for), a table (Day | Exercise | Minutes | Success check) laying out a 14-day plan, and a callout on how to self-record and compare against a native model.

tools.title: Virelangues
tools.subtitle: Tongue twisters for one sound
tools.prompt: Give 5 {difficulty} French tongue twisters targeting {sound}. Sections: cards (twister with IPA, meta = speed goal · meaning in English), steps for building speed without losing the sound, and a quote with the classic one every French child knows for this sound.
